note: The site becomes a map with three ways to read it (list, table, network). Five sections named for what you do (listen, read, use, play, guess), ten hubs with their own launching pages, and everything built since May: games, a midterms model, an ear trainer, a lab.

lines.name: listen
lines.blurb: Records, and the instruments for making or hearing them.

lines.name: read
lines.blurb: Essays, lessons, and reports: words arranged around numbers.

lines.name: use
lines.blurb: Tools that run in a browser and take your assumptions seriously.

lines.name: play
lines.blurb: Games. Some of them are also experiments, and they will tell you so.

lines.name: guess
lines.blurb: Forecasts and the methods behind them. Wrong in known ways.

hubs.name: music
hubs.lede: One album is out: fragments from a past life, glued together. Two more are garage noises begging for preservation.

hubs.name: instruments
hubs.h1: tools for making noise, and for hearing it.
hubs.lede: A fretboard, an ear trainer, and a map of where one studio’s signal goes. The ear trainer keeps score, so it is the only thing on this site that will judge you.

hubs.name: essays
hubs.h1: things I looked at long enough to write down.
hubs.lede: Data essays and the occasional argument. A few are published. Most are written, built, and waiting for me to stop fiddling with them.

hubs.name: explainers
hubs.lede: Interactive lessons that show every step of a calculation, for anyone who was once told it was obvious.

hubs.name: work
hubs.lede: Research from the day job: DORA reports, papers, and a blog post arguing that documentation matters, which it does.

hubs.name: tools
hubs.lede: Put in what you believe, including how unsure you are, and get back what that implies. Most of them run a few thousand simulations so you do not have to.

hubs.name: lab
hubs.h1: things that ask questions and keep the answers.
hubs.lede: Research platforms and experiments with language models. Most are invite-only or not deployed, because they store what people tell them, and that deserves more care than a weekend.

hubs.name: games
hubs.h1: games, for a loose definition of fun.
hubs.lede: Three games started in September: a political economy for four players, a war fought through late reports, and a survival game played behind a veil of ignorance. None are open to the public yet.

hubs.name: forecasts
hubs.lede: Election models and one football model. The 2026 midterms model refits every day, whether or not anything happened.

hubs.name: methods
hubs.lede: Research code for estimating things that resist being estimated. Mostly R. Mostly unfinished.

things.title: cheap sensationalism
things.blurb: Fragments from a past life glued together, leaving a couple moments of conceivable musicality.

things.title: chords & lyrics
things.note: written out once already, on an older version of this site
things.blurb: The chords and words to cheap sensationalism, so you can get it wrong at home.

things.title: philadelphia demos
things.blurb: Historic, revolutionary, British, Quaker, unfinished.

things.title: slop
things.blurb: Garage noises begging for preservation.

things.title: more, more, more
things.blurb: Coming soon, according to a banner that has said so since May.

things.title: the fretboard
things.blurb: Scales, chords, and modes laid out on a guitar neck, so you can see where your hand is supposed to go.

things.title: ear commander
things.blurb: Ear training for intervals, chords, scales, and modes that scores you against chance, which is less flattering than it sounds. Nothing you do leaves your device.

things.title: the patchbay
things.note: in service for one studio: mine
things.blurb: An interactive map of how one studio’s signal runs through Logic, with each plugin’s settings drawn as curves. Built to mix slop.

things.title: earcraft
things.blurb: An earlier ear trainer that tied notes to colours and intervals to plants. Ear Commander replaced it and keeps score instead.

things.title: weird weather
things.blurb: How strange was your city’s winter? Every city measured against its own history, with a model underneath.

things.title: virtue, vice & search trends
things.note: built and audited; not published yet
things.blurb: Which Google searches rise and fall around New Year’s, from 2005 to now, with the corrections for multiple comparisons that the resolutions themselves never get.

things.title: all you need is…
things.blurb: A theory of the Beatles’ emotional arc, tested two ways: topic models, and AI coders reading every song. The lyrics themselves are not reproduced.

things.title: the media story
things.blurb: Act one of a post mortem on the 2024 election, built on a survey of 153 US adults: where their news came from.

things.title: party alignment
things.blurb: Act two: how closely people’s positions matched the party they voted for. It ends by looking ahead to 2026 and 2028.

things.title: belief systems
things.blurb: Act three: worldviews. Exploratory, and built on 65 people, which it says out loud.

things.title: when the only tool you have is a hammer
things.blurb: Copying code written for one election to predict a different one, and what broke.

things.title: bayes, splines & 2024 US election polls
things.blurb: Hierarchical Bayesian splines fitted to the 2024 polls, written up while the polls were still arguing.

things.title: follow-up on the bayes/splines election model
things.blurb: What the model got right and wrong, once there were votes to check it against.

things.title: taxes: where people want money to go, and where it goes
things.blurb: Where people say they want tax money to go, set beside where it actually goes.

things.title: communities, ew!
things.blurb: An essay about communities, written by someone who flinches at the word.

things.title: just how easily could we drown in slop?
things.blurb: A question about how much machine-made filler the internet can absorb, asked by someone with an album called Slop.

things.title: show your work
things.blurb: Scrolling lessons that draw each statistical calculation step by step and compute it live: ANOVA, Bayes, DAGs, GLMs, survival, machine learning, calculus.

things.title: really cool ideas
things.blurb: Eleven ideas, from thermodynamics to Freud to Foucault, each drawn as a structure you can poke and a model you can run.

things.title: predictive processing
things.blurb: The theory that a brain is mostly guessing, taught from the concepts through the maths to the arguments against it.

things.title: bayesian priors: the silent killer
things.blurb: Pick a model and a prior, and see what it believes before it has seen any data. Then see how much data it takes to change its mind.

things.title: the paradox of tragedy: a light explanation
things.note: runs on simulated data, so it explains a method, not a finding
things.blurb: Why sad songs feel good. One proposed answer, existential isolation, and the Bayesian mediation model that would test it.

things.title: causal inference: the lifesaving nerd
things.blurb: Four lessons on telling cause from coincidence: covariates, propensity scores, instrumental and mechanistic variables, and machine learning.

things.title: DORA reports
things.blurb: The yearly DORA research reports on how software gets built and what helps.

things.title: DORA’s inaugural AI capabilities model
things.blurb: The announcement of DORA’s first AI capabilities model.

things.title: documents are like sunshine
things.blurb: A deep dive into documentation, from the 2022 State of DevOps report.

things.title: AI interaction experiment
things.blurb: A paper, listed on Google Scholar.

things.title: prototyping probabilistic failure
things.blurb: A paper, listed on Google Scholar.

things.title: decision space
things.blurb: Compare two choices on up to five things you care about, each with its own uncertainty, and let a few thousand simulated futures argue it out.

things.title: decision workbench
things.blurb: The four steps of Bayesian decision analysis, decision trees included, as something you click through instead of read about.

things.title: decision process, the R version
things.blurb: The original Shiny app behind Decision Space. Retired, still standing.

things.title: where to be
things.blurb: Ranks 41 US regions by what you say matters, then carries your uncertainty about those weights through a Monte Carlo, because nobody knows exactly how much they care about trails.

things.title: being and time (and distance) in nyc
things.blurb: How walkable New York is from every subway station: heatmaps, nearest stations, travel times. The only literal subway map on this subway map.

things.title: mixed model power explorer
things.blurb: Simulates the power of a longitudinal study before you run it, plus the chance your estimate comes out with the wrong sign or the wrong size.

things.title: see power run: simplified power dynamics (or the many ways to lose)
things.blurb: People, resources, and the state of the world, simulated to see how influence moves. Currently a stub with ambitions.

things.title: updraft
things.note: prototype, waiting in a pull request
things.blurb: The evidence-based practice cycle, ask, acquire, appraise, apply, assess, with a Bayesian belief engine keeping track of what you now think.

things.title: philosophy of AI
things.blurb: The same thought experiments put to people and to AI models, with every answer pooled into one dataset. The ship of Theseus is involved.

things.title: experimentes
things.note: studies need ethics approval before anyone sees them
things.blurb: A platform for running online studies: consent, survey, debrief, and balanced assignment to conditions.

things.title: threefold
things.blurb: One app with three rooms: Noise for song sketches, Words for manuscripts, Screen for screenplays, and a reader in the corner that comments on all of them.

things.title: linguathread
things.blurb: A language-practice partner that corrects every line you write, then sums up the session.

things.title: vibe cooking
things.blurb: Say what you feel like eating. It suggests ingredients, then recipes, then a grocery list that respects your allergies.

things.title: pulse
things.note: stays closed until it has a privacy policy
things.blurb: A polling app with a review queue and a portal for researchers.

things.title: waypoint
things.blurb: Turns a goal into a plan in seven stages, then checks on it.

things.title: power & prosperity
things.blurb: A political economy for four players: business, workers, and two parties, all trying to get what they want out of the same tax code.

things.title: fog
things.note: practice mode works; online play does not yet
things.blurb: Command an army through reports that arrive late and are sometimes wrong.

things.title: lord of the dots
things.note: playable; the research version comes next
things.blurb: A ten-minute survival game played behind a Rawlsian veil of ignorance: you help write the rules before you find out which dot you are.

things.title: 2026 midterms
things.blurb: Every public poll of the 2026 midterms, run through two Bayesian models every day, with prediction markets and op-eds tracked alongside for comparison.

things.title: nfl meta-model
things.blurb: Game statistics and gradient-boosted models, compared against the bookmakers’ odds, which is the only honest benchmark.

things.title: 2025 NYC mayor
things.blurb: A poll model for the 2025 mayoral race that got as far as cleaning the data. The election happened anyway.

things.title: compound effects
things.blurb: Turning cheap, short-term effects into estimates of long-term outcomes by chaining posteriors together.

things.title: causal calc
things.blurb: The probability that a cause was necessary, sufficient, or both.

things.title: evolving clusters
things.blurb: Clustering where the cluster centres evolve, the way a genetic algorithm would.

things.title: qual network
things.blurb: A pipeline for qualitative data: tagging, reliability checks, and Bayesian networks, tested so far on synthetic data.

detours.blurb: Look out a stranger’s window somewhere in the world. Oddly calming.

detours.blurb: Every music genre mapped and playable. Algorithmic cartography of sound.

detours.blurb: Delightful interactive toys. Spend a billion dollars. Draw a perfect circle.

detours.blurb: Visual essays on culture. Data journalism that actually slaps.
